name: Content Quality
description: Measures content depth of the page's main content area by word count against page-type-specific thresholds, plus paragraph structure. AI answer engines prefer substantive, well-structured pages they can quote and ground answers in; thin or empty pages (e.g. unhydrated SPAs) give them nothing to use.
inputs: document.title and first <h1> text (page type detection)
main content element text (rendered DOM, innerText)

scoring.summary:
Start at 5. Detect page type (URL path segments, then title, then any top-level JSON-LD node, else general) and select word-count thresholds. Extract main content text (first match of main, article (all top-level articles when no main), [role=main], .content, .main-content, #content, #main; else body), skip boilerplate, count words of the visible text. Deduct 3 / 2 / 1 for very thin (< floor(min*0.33)) / thin (< floor(min*0.66)) / below minimum. Deduct 0.5 if fewer than 3 document-wide

with > 50 chars while wordCount > 200. If wordCount < 50, cap score at 1. Score = max(0, round to 1 decimal); the engine floors it and derives status from the integer.

rules.step: page type by URL path segments (lowercased, .html/.htm/.php stripped from each segment); a keyword matches a segment equal to it or starting with keyword + '-' or '_'; first match wins

rules.condition: a segment equal to 'blog', 'article', 'post' or 'news' is followed by another segment
a segment equals 'blog' (listing, with or without trailing slash)
any top-level JSON-LD node (any block, @graph members, any whitespace) has @type Article, BlogPosting or NewsArticle
any top-level JSON-LD node has @type Product

first element matching, in order: 'main', 'article', '[role="main"]', '.content', '.main-content', '#content', '#main' (for 'article', every article not nested in another article); fallback body. Skip subtrees matching: nav, header, footer, aside, .nav, .navigation, .menu, .sidebar, .header, .footer, .advertisement, .ad, script, style, noscript, iframe, [role="navigation"], [role="banner"], [role="contentinfo"], plus hidden / aria-hidden / inline display:none elements. Words = split on /\s+/, non-empty.

count of ALL document

whose innerText.trim().length > 50 is < 3 AND wordCount > 200
lists (ul, ol), li count, heading count (h1-h6), qualityIndicators {hasLists, hasMultipleHeadings >=3, hasSubstantialParagraphs >=3, hasGoodWordCount >=300}, hasGoodStructure (unused)
score = max(0, round(score*10)/10); the engine floors it

scoring.status_mapping: Engine rule on the floored score: >= 4 pass (80%), >= 3 warning (50%), else fail.

detect.source_procedure: Runs on the built HTML in the served root (static HTML, or build output for Astro/Hugo/Eleventy/Next export/Vite). Page type from the file's URL path, <title> and JSON-LD; main content text from the parsed HTML with an innerText approximation (hidden attribute, aria-hidden and inline display:none excluded). CMS stacks and unbuilt sites are skipped. For a Vite SPA the built index.html is usually an empty shell and scores as such (that is what non-JS agents get).
detect.llm_criteria: Only needed when content is produced by components or data (CMS, JSON, MDX components) that a script cannot flatten: estimate the visible word count of the main content (excluding nav, header, footer, aside, sidebar, ads) and the number of paragraphs longer than about 50 characters, then apply the same numeric thresholds. Do not judge prose quality; the extension does not.

parity.note:
The extension counts words from the rendered DOM using innerText, which excludes hidden (display:none) text and includes JS-rendered content; source counting may include hidden text and miss client-rendered or CMS-fetched content. Page type depends on the live URL (permalinks, trailing slashes, i18n prefixes) and document.title after templating. The paragraph count is document-wide including nav/footer

. Templates with variables or components make exact word counts approximate.

fix_summary:
Expand thin pages to at least the page-type minimum (e.g. 200 general, 500 article, 150 homepage/product) and break long text into 3+ real

paragraphs; wrap the primary content in

or
in the layout so boilerplate is excluded. The plugin can add the
wrapper automatically but the added content must be written or approved by the user.

divergences.extension: URL page-type rules are substring matches ('/aboutface' is about, '/helpers' is faq) and '/blog/' (a listing with a trailing slash) is typed article.
divergences.plugin: Keywords match whole path segments (or a segment starting with keyword + '-' / '_'); article needs a segment after blog/article/post/news, so '/blog/' is typed blog.
divergences.reason: Substring matching mis-typed normal URLs and the listing page, giving them the wrong thresholds.

divergences.extension: Schema page type reads only the FIRST ld+json block and requires the exact no-whitespace substring '"@type":"Article"'.
divergences.plugin: Every top-level JSON-LD node (all blocks, @graph members, any formatting) is checked for Article, BlogPosting, NewsArticle or Product.
divergences.reason: Pretty-printed and @graph JSON-LD, the common case, was missed.

divergences.extension: When there is no <main>, only the first <article> is counted, so a page of article cards is measured by one card.
divergences.plugin: All top-level <article> elements are counted together.
divergences.reason: Card listings were flagged as thin content although they are not.

divergences.extension: Words come from innerText of the rendered DOM (CSS-hidden text excluded, JS-rendered text included).
divergences.plugin: Words come from the built HTML with an innerText approximation (hidden, aria-hidden and inline display:none excluded; stylesheet-hidden text included; JS-rendered text absent).
divergences.reason: Source-vs-live: the plugin reads the repo. The built HTML is what non-JS crawlers see.

divergences.extension: Status comes from the unfloored score (e.g. 4.5 is pass) while the reported score is floored.
divergences.plugin: Status is derived from the reported integer score by the shared 80% / 50% rule.
